terms.explanation: What a trade made or lost once every fee is taken off.
What a trade made or lost from the price move alone, before any fee is taken off.
What the exchange charges you each time you buy or sell.
Your results after fees from every closed trade, added up day by day from your first result to today.
A picture of how the results of your closed trades add up over time; realized means the trade is closed, so its result is final.
An entry is a buy or sell that starts or adds to a trade, and an exit is one that closes part or all of it, each with its own price, amount and time.
A trade you describe only by when it opened and closed; Kairos estimates its prices from the market's candles at those times, so they are not your real prices.
Your result divided by what you would have lost at your stop, so +2× means you won twice what you risked and −1× means you lost exactly what you risked.
How far your target is from your entry compared with how far your stop is, so 2× means the possible win is twice the possible loss.
The price where you plan to get out if the trade goes against you; it decides how much you can lose.
The price where you plan to take your win if the trade goes your way.
How much of a coin or other asset you buy or sell in one trade.
Using borrowed money so your trade is bigger than the money in your account; at 5× every price move changes your account five times as much, losses as well as wins.
One bar on a price chart that shows where the price started, its highest and lowest points, and where it ended during one stretch of time.
A trade that buys first and makes money when the price goes up.
A trade that sells first and buys back later, so it makes money when the price goes down.
The usual small step of a currency pair's price: 0.0001 for most pairs and 0.01 when the price is in Japanese yen (JPY). EUR/USD moving from 1.0850 to 1.0860 is 10 pips.
A set amount of a pair's first currency: 1 lot is 100,000 units, a mini lot 10,000 and a micro lot 1,000. Kairos saves your size in units, so 0.1 lots is saved as 10,000.

The short code of a company's shares on a stock exchange, such as AAPL for Apple. Some end with a dot and a code for the exchange, such as 7203.T in Tokyo or VOD.L in London. Kairos saves the ticker in capital letters and never guesses its currency from it.

A small piece of a company that you can buy and sell. A stock's price is the price of one share, and Quantity is the number of shares you trade. Many brokers also sell parts of a share, such as 0.5 of a share.

How much of one currency one unit of another is worth on a given day, such as 1 EUR = 1.146 USD. Kairos uses it only to show your totals in your own currency; each trade keeps the currency you recorded.
